title: Production and uses of NPK fertilisers

notes.definition: NPK fertilisers are formulations of various salts containing appropriate percentages of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium compounds. They are used to improve agricultural productivity and are made industrially from ammonia, nitric acid, sulfuric acid, phosphate rock and mined potassium salts in integrated processes.
explanation: Compounds of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are used as fertilisers to improve agricultural productivity. Plants need these elements for healthy growth, and they are removed from the soil when crops are harvested. NPK fertilisers contain compounds of all three elements. They are formulations (carefully designed mixtures) of various salts containing appropriate percentages of the elements, and the ratio can be chosen to suit the crop and soil.

Industrial production of NPK fertilisers can be achieved using a variety of raw materials in several integrated processes. Ammonia from the Haber process can be used to manufacture ammonium salts and nitric acid. Ammonia reacts with nitric acid to form ammonium nitrate: NH₃ + HNO₃ → NH₄NO₃. Ammonia reacts with sulfuric acid to form ammonium sulfate: 2NH₃ + H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄. Ammonia reacts with phosphoric acid to form ammonium phosphate: 3NH₃ + H₃PO₄ → (NH₄)₃PO₄. Ammonium phosphate supplies both nitrogen and phosphorus.

Potassium chloride, potassium sulfate and phosphate rock are obtained by mining. Potassium chloride and potassium sulfate are soluble and can be used directly as a source of potassium. However, phosphate rock (mainly calcium phosphate) cannot be used directly as a fertiliser because it is insoluble, so plants cannot absorb it. Phosphate rock is treated with acid to produce soluble salts that can be used as fertilisers.

When phosphate rock is treated with nitric acid it produces phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate. When it is treated with sulfuric acid it produces single superphosphate, a mixture of calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate. When it is treated with phosphoric acid it produces triple superphosphate, which is calcium phosphate. These products are more soluble than the original rock and can be used in fertilisers (the phosphoric acid can also be neutralised with ammonia to make ammonium phosphate).

You should be able to compare industrial production of fertilisers with laboratory preparations of the same compounds. In the laboratory, ammonium sulfate is made on a small scale by titrating dilute ammonia solution with dilute sulfuric acid to find the exact volumes for neutralisation, then repeating without indicator and crystallising the salt by evaporating the water. This is a batch process using purchased chemicals. In industry, the same salt is made on a huge scale in a continuous process, from raw materials made on site (ammonia from the Haber process, sulfuric acid from the Contact process), using concentrated reactants, with several stages linked together; heat released by the exothermic neutralisation can be used to evaporate water.
keyFacts: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium compounds are used as fertilisers to improve agricultural productivity.
NPK fertilisers are formulations of salts containing appropriate percentages of N, P and K.
Ammonia is used to make ammonium salts and nitric acid.
Ammonia + nitric acid → ammonium nitrate; ammonia + sulfuric acid → ammonium sulfate; ammonia + phosphoric acid → ammonium phosphate.
Potassium chloride, potassium sulfate and phosphate rock are obtained by mining.
Phosphate rock cannot be used directly as it is insoluble.
Phosphate rock + nitric acid → phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate.
Phosphate rock + sulfuric acid → single superphosphate (calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate).
Phosphate rock + phosphoric acid → triple superphosphate (calcium phosphate).
Lab preparation: small scale, batch, titration then crystallisation. Industry: large scale, continuous, integrated processes.

keyTerms.definition: A substance added to soil to provide elements that plants need for growth, improving crop yields.
A fertiliser containing compounds of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
A mixture designed as a useful product, with each component in a measured quantity.
A mined rock containing calcium phosphate; insoluble, so it is treated with acid to make fertilisers.
A mixture of calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate, made by treating phosphate rock with sulfuric acid.
Calcium phosphate made by treating phosphate rock with phosphoric acid.
Several linked industrial processes, where the product of one is the raw material for another.
A process in which reactants are fed in and products removed all the time, rather than in separate batches.

equations.name: Percentage by mass of an element in a compound
equations.formula: % by mass = (Ar × number of atoms of the element ÷ Mr of compound) × 100

workedExamples.title: Percentage of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate
workedExamples.question: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃. (Ar: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16)

workedExamples.title: Comparing fertilisers
workedExamples.question: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄, and compare it with ammonium nitrate (35%). (Ar: N = 14, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
workedExamples.answer: 21.2%; ammonium nitrate supplies more nitrogen per kilogram.

workedExamples.title: Mass of ammonium nitrate from ammonia
workedExamples.question: Calculate the mass of ammonium nitrate that can be made from 34 tonnes of ammonia. NH₃ + HNO₃ → NH₄NO₃ (Mr: NH₃ = 17, NH₄NO₃ = 80)
steps: 1 mol NH₃ gives 1 mol NH₄NO₃, so 17 tonnes gives 80 tonnes.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think phosphate rock can be spread straight onto fields.
misconceptions.right: In fact phosphate rock is insoluble, so plants cannot absorb it; it must be treated with acid to make soluble salts.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think NPK fertilisers contain the pure elements nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
misconceptions.right: In fact they contain soluble compounds (salts) of these elements, such as ammonium nitrate and potassium chloride.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think laboratory and industrial methods use the same scale and process.
misconceptions.right: In fact the lab uses small-scale batch titration and crystallisation, while industry uses large-scale continuous, integrated processes with concentrated reactants.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think potassium salts are made in the Haber process.
misconceptions.right: In fact potassium chloride and potassium sulfate are obtained by mining.

realWorld: Fertiliser bags show the N:P:K ratio, for example 20-10-10, so farmers can choose the right formulation for each crop.
Ammonium nitrate is one of the most widely used nitrogen fertilisers in the UK.
Potash (potassium salts) is mined in North Yorkshire for use in fertilisers.

flashcards.front: Which three elements do NPK fertilisers supply?

flashcards.back: To improve agricultural productivity (increase crop yields).
A mixture designed as a useful product with components in measured quantities.

flashcards.front: Which fertiliser raw materials are mined?
flashcards.back: Potassium chloride, potassium sulfate and phosphate rock.

questions.question: What do the letters NPK stand for in NPK fertilisers?
questions.explanation: K is the symbol for potassium (from kalium); P is phosphorus; N is nitrogen.

questions.question: Which salt is formed when ammonia reacts with nitric acid?
questions.explanation: Nitric acid gives nitrate salts: NH₃ + HNO₃ → NH₄NO₃.

questions.question: Which of these is obtained by mining?
questions.explanation: Potassium chloride, potassium sulfate and phosphate rock are mined. Ammonia and nitric acid are manufactured.

questions.question: Why is phosphate rock treated with acid before it is used as a fertiliser?
options: To convert it into soluble salts that plants can absorb
markScheme: 1 mark: to make soluble salts that plants can absorb
questions.explanation: Phosphate rock is insoluble, so plants cannot take up the phosphorus from it.

questions.question: What is produced when phosphate rock is treated with sulfuric acid?
options: Single superphosphate (calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate)
markScheme: 1 mark: single superphosphate (calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate)
questions.explanation: Phosphoric acid gives triple superphosphate; nitric acid gives phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate.

questions.question: What is produced when phosphate rock is treated with nitric acid?
markScheme: 1 mark: phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate
questions.explanation: The calcium in the rock forms calcium nitrate and the phosphate is released as phosphoric acid.

questions.question: Which fertiliser supplies both nitrogen and phosphorus?
questions.explanation: (NH₄)₃PO₄ contains N in the ammonium ions and P in the phosphate ion.

questions.question: Which is a feature of the industrial production of ammonium sulfate, but not of its laboratory preparation?
options: Using a burette to add acid
A continuous process using concentrated reactants on a large scale
Crystallising the salt by evaporating water
markScheme: 1 mark: continuous process using concentrated reactants on a large scale
questions.explanation: Labs use small-scale batch titrations with dilute solutions; industry runs continuous, large-scale processes.

questions.question: What is triple superphosphate?
options: A mixture of calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate
Calcium phosphate made by treating phosphate rock with phosphoric acid
markScheme: 1 mark: calcium phosphate made from phosphate rock and phosphoric acid
questions.explanation: Single superphosphate is the mixture with calcium sulfate, made using sulfuric acid.

questions.question:
Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃.
Relative atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1, O = 16
questions.explanation: There are two nitrogen atoms in NH₄NO₃: one in NH₄⁺ and one in NO₃⁻. Using only one gives 17.5%, a common error.

questions.question:
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄.
Relative atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16
questions.explanation: The bracket means two NH₄ groups: 2 × 18 = 36; 36 + 32 + 4 × 16 = 132.

questions.question:
Calculate the percentage by mass of phosphorus in ammonium phosphate, (NH₄)₃PO₄. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
Relative atomic masses: N = 14, H = 1, P = 31, O = 16
A farmer needs to add 70 kg of nitrogen to a field. Ammonium nitrate contains 35% nitrogen by mass. Calculate the mass of ammonium nitrate needed.
questions.explanation: Mass of fertiliser × 0.35 = 70 kg, so mass = 70 ÷ 0.35 = 200 kg.

questions.question:
Calculate the mass of ammonium nitrate that can be made from 8.5 tonnes of ammonia.
NH₃ + HNO₃ → NH₄NO₃
Relative formula masses: NH₃ = 17, NH₄NO₃ = 80
markScheme: 1 mark: 17 tonnes gives 80 tonnes (1:1 mole ratio)
questions.explanation: 8.5 is half of 17, so half of 80 = 40 tonnes.

questions.question: A student prepares ammonium sulfate in the laboratory. The maximum theoretical mass is 6.60 g. The student obtains 4.95 g of dry crystals. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.explanation: Some product is lost during crystallisation and filtering, so the yield is less than 100%.

questions.question: A 50 kg bag of NPK fertiliser is labelled 20% N. Calculate the mass of nitrogen in the bag.
questions.explanation: 20% of 50 kg = 10 kg.

questions.question: State why farmers add fertilisers to soil.
markScheme: 1 mark: to improve agricultural productivity / increase crop yields / replace elements removed by crops
questions.explanation: Harvesting crops removes N, P and K from the soil.

questions.question: Name the acid that reacts with ammonia to make ammonium sulfate, and write the formula of ammonium sulfate.
questions.explanation: 2NH₃ + H₂SO₄ → (NH₄)₂SO₄.

questions.question: Name two potassium compounds that are mined for use in fertilisers.
questions.explanation: These are soluble and can be used directly as a source of potassium.

questions.question: Explain why phosphate rock cannot be used directly as a fertiliser and how it is made suitable.
markScheme: 1 mark: phosphate rock is insoluble so plants cannot absorb it
1 mark: it is treated with (nitric, sulfuric or phosphoric) acid to produce soluble salts
questions.explanation: Plants absorb nutrients as dissolved ions through their roots.

questions.question: Name the products formed when phosphate rock is treated with: (a) nitric acid, (b) sulfuric acid, (c) phosphoric acid.
markScheme: 1 mark: (a) phosphoric acid and calcium nitrate
1 mark: (b) single superphosphate / calcium phosphate and calcium sulfate
questions.explanation: These are the salts the specification requires you to recall.

questions.question: Write a balanced equation for the reaction of ammonia with phosphoric acid to make ammonium phosphate.
questions.explanation: Phosphoric acid has three hydrogen ions to neutralise, so three ammonia molecules are needed.

questions.question: Ammonium sulfate contains 21.2% nitrogen and ammonium nitrate contains 35% nitrogen. Suggest why a farmer might still choose ammonium sulfate.
markScheme: 1 mark: ammonium sulfate also supplies sulfur, which some crops/soils need
1 mark: it may be cheaper per kg of nitrogen
1 mark: ammonium nitrate is more hazardous to store (can be explosive)
questions.explanation: Choosing a fertiliser involves more than percentage of nitrogen: cost, other nutrients and safety matter too.

questions.question:
Ammonium sulfate can be made in a school laboratory and in industry.
Compare the laboratory preparation of ammonium sulfate with its industrial production.
markScheme: Indicative content: Laboratory: small scale (grams); batch process; dilute ammonia solution and dilute sulfuric acid bought from suppliers; titration with indicator to find volumes, then repeat without indicator; evaporate some water and leave to crystallise; filter and dry crystals; heat supplied by Bunsen burner or water bath; few stages. Industry: very large scale (tonnes per day); continuous process; raw materials made on site in integrated processes (ammonia from Haber process, sulfuric acid from Contact process); concentrated reactants; exothermic neutralisation heat used to evaporate water; automated control; product often made into granules; several linked stages.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed comparison covering scale, batch versus continuous, source and concentration of reactants, method of separation and energy, with clear comparative statements.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): describes both methods with some comparison.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about one method.
questions.explanation: A comparison needs linking words such as 'whereas' for each point.

questions.question: Describe how the raw materials ammonia, sulfuric acid, nitric acid, phosphate rock and potassium chloride can be used to produce an NPK fertiliser.
markScheme: Indicative content: ammonia reacts with nitric acid to make ammonium nitrate (N) and with sulfuric acid to make ammonium sulfate (N); phosphate rock (insoluble, mined) treated with nitric acid or sulfuric acid to give soluble phosphate salts (P), for example single superphosphate; phosphoric acid neutralised with ammonia gives ammonium phosphate (N and P); potassium chloride is mined and supplies K; salts mixed in suitable proportions to make a formulation.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): describes how N, P and K are each provided, with correct named products and the idea of a formulation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): describes one or two reactions or sources.
questions.explanation: Make sure each of N, P and K is accounted for.

questions.question: What is an NPK fertiliser?
options: A formulation of salts containing nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium
A single compound containing only nitrogen
markScheme: 1 mark: a formulation of salts containing N, P and K
questions.explanation: NPK fertilisers are mixtures of various salts in suitable percentages.

questions.question: State which element is supplied to plants by potassium chloride.
questions.explanation: Potassium chloride is the K in NPK.

questions.question: Why is producing ammonium nitrate described as part of an integrated process?
options: Both reactants, ammonia and nitric acid, are made on the same site, and nitric acid is itself made from ammonia
It only needs one raw material
It is done by hand in small batches
It does not need any energy
markScheme: 1 mark: reactants made on site; nitric acid made from ammonia
questions.explanation: In integrated processes the product of one process is the raw material for another, reducing transport and cost.
